title: Minimum Incompatibility
summary: Given an integer array and an integer k, distribute the array into k equal-sized subsets with no equal elements in the same subset.
statement: Given an integer array and an integer k, distribute the array into k equal-sized subsets with no equal elements in the same subset. Calculate the minimum sum of the differences between the maximum and minimum elements in each subset. Return -1 if distribution is impossible.
constraints: nums has at most 16 positive integers and its length is divisible by k.
Partition all positions into k equal-size groups; duplicate values may not appear within one group.
A group costs max-min. Return the minimum total cost, or -1 when no valid partition exists.
hints: Treat positions as distinct bits even when their values repeat.
Precompute every duplicate-free subset of one group size and its max-minus-min cost.
DP over used-position masks, requiring each next group to contain the first unused position to avoid group-order duplicates.
Every valid partition has exactly one sequence under the first-unused rule, and minimizing the sum over all compatible group subsets examines every partition.
editorial: Every valid partition has exactly one sequence under the first-unused rule, and minimizing the sum over all compatible group subsets examines every partition.

tests.explanation: Groups [1,2] and [1,4] cost one and three, totaling four.
Four duplicate-free pairs can be selected with total incompatibility six.
